commit_message:
[Runtime] Honor the base argument in atoi_int32_base (#24677)

### Problem
`iree_string_view_atoi_int32_base` ignores its `base` argument.

### Root cause
`runtime/src/iree/base/string_view.c:387` calls `strtol(temp, &end, 0)`
— the `base` parameter is never used, so any requested radix is silently
discarded and the string is parsed with C auto-detection (leading `0x` →
hex, leading `0` → octal, else decimal). The three sibling `_base`
functions forward the argument correctly: `strtoul(temp, &end, base)`
(uint32, :413), `strtoll(..., base)` (int64, :436), `strtoull(...,
base)` (uint64, :462). The non-`base` wrapper
`iree_string_view_atoi_int32` already passes `0` explicitly (:399), so
the `_base` variant is clearly meant to honor a caller-supplied radix. A
caller requesting base 16 or 2 gets wrong values (e.g. base=16 `"10"` →
10 instead of 16).

### Fix
Forward `base` to `strtol`, matching the sibling `_base` functions.

### Verification
Static reasoning + sibling consistency; trivially checkable:
`strtol("10", &e, 16) == 16` vs the current `strtol("10", &e, 0) == 10`.
(No full runtime build on my machine — happy to add a unit test if
useful.)

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>

`iree_string_view_atoi_int32_base` ignores its `base` argument.

### Root cause
`runtime/src/iree/base/string_view.c:387` calls `strtol(temp, &end, 0)`
— the `base` parameter is never used, so any requested radix is silently
discarded and the string is parsed with C auto-detection (leading `0x` →
hex, leading `0` → octal, else decimal). The three sibling `_base`
functions forward the argument correctly: `strtoul(temp, &end, base)`
(uint32, :413), `strtoll(..., base)` (int64, :436), `strtoull(...,
base)` (uint64, :462). The non-`base` wrapper
`iree_string_view_atoi_int32` already passes `0` explicitly (:399), so
the `_base` variant is clearly meant to honor a caller-supplied radix. A
caller requesting base 16 or 2 gets wrong values (e.g. base=16 `"10"` →
10 instead of 16).

### Fix
Forward `base` to `strtol`, matching the sibling `_base` functions.

### Verification
Static reasoning + sibling consistency; trivially checkable:
`strtol("10", &e, 16) == 16` vs the current `strtol("10", &e, 0) == 10`.
(No full runtime build on my machine — happy to add a unit test if
useful.)

commit_message:
[Preprocessing] Guard rank-reduced insert_slice in strided-insert conversions

ConvertStridedInsertSliceToGeneric and SwapStridedInsertSliceWithContraction
index the insert_slice source with a destination-rank dim index (the
reassociation groups / strided-dim loop are derived from the destination).
tensor.insert_slice allows a rank-reduced source, and a non-unit stride on a
dropped unit dim still verifies, so for such input the index runs past the
source shape (OOB: assert crash in asserts builds, garbage read in release).
Both algorithms assume source dim i == dest dim i, so decline the
rank-reduced case with a rank-equality check; the intended equal-rank cases
are unaffected.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Reject negative ragged_dim in cast_to_ragged_shape verifier

CastToRaggedShapeOp::verify reads raggedDim via getSExtValue() and only
checks raggedDim >= sourceRank. A negative raggedDim (e.g. ragged_dim(-1))
then flows into resultType.isDynamicDim(raggedDim)/getDimSize(raggedDim),
which take an unsigned index, so -1 reads past the shape (the idx < rank
assert is debug-only). The op's documented constraint is
0 <= ragged_dim < rank(source). Reject negatives before indexing.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[InputConversion][TOSA]: change TOSA level to none (#24667)

For some TOSA lowering use-cases, we will have dynamic batch sizes and
this will trigger the level check. Here we set the level to none so that
dynamic dimensions are allowed in TOSA IR.

The TOSA level check ensures that tensor sizes are within a certain
threshold but for our use-case with TFlite this is not always the case.

---

commit_message:
[Flow] Fix out-of-bounds write in flow.tensor.update folder

tensorUpdate() writes targetValues[getFlattenedIndex(targetType, targetIndex)]
where targetIndex starts at the constant start_indices and advances by the
update extents. getFlattenedIndex applies no bounds clamping, so when
start_indices[j] + update_dim[j] > target_dim[j] the flattened offset runs
past targetValues (OOB write; asserts are off in release builds).
TensorUpdateOp::verify does not reject such updates, so a 2x2 update at
offset [2,3] into a 3x4 target passes verification and hits this during
canonicalization. Decline to fold when the update does not fit within the
target, mirroring the sibling non-foldable path.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Flow] Fix out-of-bounds write in flow.tensor.update folder

tensorUpdate() writes targetValues[getFlattenedIndex(targetType, targetIndex)]
where targetIndex starts at the constant start_indices and advances by the
update extents. getFlattenedIndex applies no bounds clamping, so when
start_indices[j] + update_dim[j] > target_dim[j] the flattened offset runs
past targetValues (OOB write; asserts are off in release builds).
TensorUpdateOp::verify does not reject such updates, so a 2x2 update at
offset [2,3] into a 3x4 target passes verification and hits this during
canonicalization. Decline to fold when the update does not fit within the
target, mirroring the sibling non-foldable path.

commit_message:
[InputConversion][TOSA]: change TOSA level to none (#24667)

For some TOSA lowering use-cases, we will have dynamic batch sizes and
this will trigger the level check. Here we set the level to none so that
dynamic dimensions are allowed in TOSA IR.

The TOSA level check ensures that tensor sizes are within a certain
threshold but for our use-case with TFlite this is not always the case.

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Fix dropped `!` in WinogradInputTransformOp rank-2 dim-1 check

The rank-2 input verification checks dim 0 with `!isDynamicDim(0) &&
getDimSize(0) > inputTileSize`, but the dim-1 clause is missing the `!`.
That makes the dim-1 branch dead: for a static dim it short-circuits before
comparing the size, and for a dynamic dim getDimSize(1) is kDynamic
(INT64_MIN) which is never > inputTileSize. A rank-2 input whose static
dim 1 exceeds the input tile size is therefore accepted, contradicting the
op's own diagnostic. Add the missing `!` to mirror the dim-0 clause.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Fix dropped `!` in WinogradInputTransformOp rank-2 dim-1 check

The rank-2 input verification checks dim 0 with `!isDynamicDim(0) &&
getDimSize(0) > inputTileSize`, but the dim-1 clause is missing the `!`.
That makes the dim-1 branch dead: for a static dim it short-circuits before
comparing the size, and for a dynamic dim getDimSize(1) is kDynamic
(INT64_MIN) which is never > inputTileSize. A rank-2 input whose static
dim 1 exceeds the input tile size is therefore accepted, contradicting the
op's own diagnostic. Add the missing `!` to mirror the dim-0 clause.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_asan / linux_x64_clang_asan

commit_message:
[InputConversion][TOSA]: change TOSA level to none (#24667)

For some TOSA lowering use-cases, we will have dynamic batch sizes and
this will trigger the level check. Here we set the level to none so that
dynamic dimensions are allowed in TOSA IR.

The TOSA level check ensures that tensor sizes are within a certain
threshold but for our use-case with TFlite this is not always the case.

commit_message:
[InputConversion][TOSA]: change TOSA level to none (#24667)

For some TOSA lowering use-cases, we will have dynamic batch sizes and
this will trigger the level check. Here we set the level to none so that
dynamic dimensions are allowed in TOSA IR.

The TOSA level check ensures that tensor sizes are within a certain
threshold but for our use-case with TFlite this is not always the case.

commit_message:
Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports
int/index/float). Creating an `arith.constant` from the null attribute
aborts the process.

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,
or index instead of crashing.

Repro:
`interesting.sh`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.
grep -q "complex.create" "$1"
```

`complex_repro.mlir`
```
// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.
//
// The linalg.generic writes a complex<f32> tensor. When the reducer decides to
// replace this op with a linalg.fill of a zero constant, it calls
// Builder::getZeroAttr(complex<f32>), which returns a null attribute. Building
// an arith.constant from that null attribute crashes ("Failed to infer result
// type(s)").
//
// The op survives the earlier reduction strategies because the interestingness
// check (interesting.sh) requires "complex.create" to remain present, so the
// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],
    iterator_types = ["parallel"]
  } ins(%arg0 : tensor<4xf32>) outs(%empty : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>) {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: complex<f32>):
    %c = complex.create %in, %in : complex<f32>
    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}
```

```bash
chmod +x interesting.sh

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports
int/index/float). Creating an `arith.constant` from the null attribute
aborts the process.

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,
or index instead of crashing.

Repro:
`interesting.sh`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.
grep -q "complex.create" "$1"
```

`complex_repro.mlir`
```
// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.
//
// The linalg.generic writes a complex<f32> tensor. When the reducer decides to
// replace this op with a linalg.fill of a zero constant, it calls
// Builder::getZeroAttr(complex<f32>), which returns a null attribute. Building
// an arith.constant from that null attribute crashes ("Failed to infer result
// type(s)").
//
// The op survives the earlier reduction strategies because the interestingness
// check (interesting.sh) requires "complex.create" to remain present, so the
// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],
    iterator_types = ["parallel"]
  } ins(%arg0 : tensor<4xf32>) outs(%empty : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>) {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: complex<f32>):
    %c = complex.create %in, %in : complex<f32>
    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}
```

chmod +x interesting.sh
iree-reduce ./interesting.sh ./complex_repro.mlir -o reduced.mlir

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports
int/index/float). Creating an `arith.constant` from the null attribute
aborts the process.

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,
or index instead of crashing.

Repro:
`interesting.sh`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.
grep -q "complex.create" "$1"
```

`complex_repro.mlir`

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.
//
// The linalg.generic writes a complex<f32> tensor. When the reducer decides to
// replace this op with a linalg.fill of a zero constant, it calls
// Builder::getZeroAttr(complex<f32>), which returns a null attribute. Building
// an arith.constant from that null attribute crashes ("Failed to infer result
// type(s)").
//
// The op survives the earlier reduction strategies because the interestingness
// check (interesting.sh) requires "complex.create" to remain present, so the
// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],
    iterator_types = ["parallel"]
  } ins(%arg0 : tensor<4xf32>) outs(%empty : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>) {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: complex<f32>):
    %c = complex.create %in, %in : complex<f32>
    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}
```

chmod +x interesting.sh
iree-reduce ./interesting.sh ./complex_repro.mlir -o reduced.mlir

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,

# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {

    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.

# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>

    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>

}

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.
grep -q "complex.create" "$1"

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

// check (interesting.sh) requires "complex.create" to remain present, so the
// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],
    iterator_types = ["parallel"]
  } ins(%arg0 : tensor<4xf32>) outs(%empty : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>) {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: complex<f32>):
    %c = complex.create %in, %in : complex<f32>
    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.

# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>

}

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.

# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

// reducer reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still in place.
func.func @main(%arg0: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>> {
  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  return %0 : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
}

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,

#!/bin/bash

# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.

# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

}

Address crash in iree-reduce with complex tensors (#24674)

See issue https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24673. Details are
repeated here.

`iree-reduce` crashes in `reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta` when it tries to
replace a `linalg` op that produces a **complex**-typed tensor. The
strategy builds a zero constant via `Builder::getZeroAttr(elementType)`,
which returns a **null** attribute for `complex` (it only supports

The proposed fix simply does an early-out if the type is not int, float,

#!/bin/bash
# Interestingness oracle for iree-reduce.
#
# A reduced candidate is "interesting" (exit 0) only while it still contains the
# complex-typed linalg.generic (identified by the complex.create in its body).
# This keeps the reducer from deleting the op via an earlier strategy, so it
# reaches reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta with the complex op still present.

// Minimal reproducer for the iree-reduce crash in reduceLinalgOnTensorsDelta.

  %empty = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>
  %0 = linalg.generic {
    indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>],

    linalg.yield %c : complex<f32>
  } -> tensor<4xcomplex<f32>>

}

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Separate ins and outs of Sort op

Currently, the Sort op is defined to take no ins() operands, and instead
takes the input tensors as outs(). After bufferization, it modifies
those outs() in-place. Not only is this inconsistent with other
LinalgExt ops, it also breaks some compiler invariants leading to bugs.

For that reason, we re-define the Sort op to take input tensors as ins()
and inits as outs(). Lit and E2E tests had to be converted to the new
syntax.

Assisted-by: Codex <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Separate ins and outs of Sort op

Currently, the Sort op is defined to take no ins() operands, and instead
takes the input tensors as outs(). After bufferization, it modifies
those outs() in-place. Not only is this inconsistent with other
LinalgExt ops, it also breaks some compiler invariants leading to bugs.

For that reason, we re-define the Sort op to take input tensors as ins()
and inits as outs(). Lit and E2E tests had to be converted to the new
syntax.

commit_message:
base/string_view: honor the base argument in atoi_int32_base

iree_string_view_atoi_int32_base ignored its `base` parameter and always
called strtol(..., 0), so a requested radix was silently discarded and the
string was parsed with C auto-detection instead. The three sibling _base
functions (uint32/int64/uint64) correctly forward the argument
(strtoul/strtoll/strtoull(..., base)), and the non-base wrapper already
passes 0 explicitly. Forward `base` so callers requesting e.g. base 16 or
2 get correct results.

Signed-off-by: Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>

commit_message:
base/string_view: honor the base argument in atoi_int32_base

iree_string_view_atoi_int32_base ignored its `base` parameter and always
called strtol(..., 0), so a requested radix was silently discarded and the
string was parsed with C auto-detection instead. The three sibling _base
functions (uint32/int64/uint64) correctly forward the argument
(strtoul/strtoll/strtoull(..., base)), and the non-base wrapper already
passes 0 explicitly. Forward `base` so callers requesting e.g. base 16 or
2 get correct results.
